ideal: It must be possible for a list to have more than three clauses and to have clauses that begin with the same subject.
note: one sentence instead of a two-item list

ideal: When a list is a rule whose two sides are each one clause and neither side begins with a time phrase, verbalizer says the list without "then".
note: merged the two time-phrase negations into "neither side"

ideal: When the formula of a unit cannot be said in words, checker says why.
note: dropped the repeated "the formula of the unit cannot be said"

ideal: Take a scenario that cannot happen while every held unit holds, and for which the author asks about leaving out no unit. For each unit whose formula the analyzer is asked to hold, some search that leaves one unit out leaves out that unit and requires the scenario to happen.
note: set up the scenario first, then one search per held unit
one shared trigger with two bullets; "until" said as "now or later ... before then"

ideal: Verbalizer says a quantifier with no fact for its variable beside another thing in full, with "there is" and the numbered name.
note: condition folded into the noun phrase

ideal: When a run asks for `generate` or `check` and the verbalizer fails on the formula of any unit with a fault of its own, the run does not exit with code 0, and checker does not say why that formula cannot be said.
note: "any unit" keeps the run and the unit independent

ideal: The statement of a unit is stale when the unit holds a formula that can be said in words, the statement sits between the markers of a generated region, and it differs from what its formula says.
note: conclusion first, conditions as one sentence

ideal: There can be a quantifier whose variable is the subject of the sentence and whose reading says the variable twice.
note: two relative clauses on one noun

ideal: When a list is a rule with a first side and a second, but not a rule whose two sides are each one clause, verbalizer says it with "then" at the start of the second side, on a line of its own.
note: "it" for the repeated list

ideal: When a list is a rule whose two sides are each one clause and whose first side does not begin with a time phrase, verbalizer says it on one line, as "when <first side>, <second side>".
note: showed the one-line shape as a template

ideal: When a definition has an alternative that says something about another unit, verbalizer says it as a list of the alternatives as they stand.
note: dropped the numbered name

ideal: A list can have three clauses or fewer and still be longer than a line when it is put in a sentence.
note: "can ... and still" for the possibility

ideal: When it generates, checker does not write the statement of a unit held by a document that the project does not list among the documents it checks, if that document is context for one the project does list.
note: the unit's statement up front, the documents as its qualifiers

ideal: There can be a scenario that cannot happen while every held unit holds, that checker reports cannot happen, and whose report names a unit whose leaving out lets the scenario happen.
note: everything hung on one scenario

ideal: When an item of a list is more than one clause, verbalizer says the list as bullets.
note: item as subject

ideal: Checker does not report the formula of a unit as lone on a word that a block of some other unit names outside its declaration.
note: "some other unit" replaces the inequality clause

ideal: When the alternatives of a definition each begin with the kind of the subject and the definition can be said kind by kind, verbalizer says it as a list with a noun phrase for each kind, such as "a spec that cites no axiom".
note: one sentence, no list

ideal: A run that asks for a check command does not exit with code 0 if checker reports the formula of any unit as lone on any word.
note: "any" keeps the unit independent of the run

ideal: When a definition has two alternatives for one kind and can be said kind by kind, verbalizer says it as one noun phrase for that kind, with the alternatives joined by or.
note: "it" for the definition

ideal: When the statement of a unit is current, checker does not report it.
note: "it" for the repeated statement

ideal: At no moment does a call in which code disposes an owner after pulse disposed it either throw or run a cleanup that code has registered on the owner and that has not run.
note: the two "always no" parts share one call

ideal: When a scenario cannot happen while every held unit holds, checker reports that it cannot happen.
note: dropped the numbered name

ideal: It must be possible that an owner has another owner H as the nearest error handler or boundary above it, and that, now or later, pulse disposes the owner while a failing cleanup is on it, then at that moment or later the cleanup runs, and at that moment or later its error has reached H.
note: a chain of "at that moment or later" instead of nested lists

ideal: When a unit holds more than one formula, its formula cannot be said in words.
note: "its" for the unit

ideal: Verbalizer says a list of more than three clauses as bullets.
note: condition folded into the noun phrase

ideal: Verbalizer says a list as bullets when it is longer than a line when put in a sentence.
note: conclusion first

ideal: When a definition has a run of and beside another alternative of its kind, verbalizer says it as a list of the alternatives as they stand.
note: dropped the numbered name

ideal: When the formula of a unit cannot be said in words, checker does not write the unit's statement when it generates.
note: possessive for the repeated unit

ideal:
A quantifier fits a noun phrase unless it is one of these:
- a quantifier whose reading says the variable twice
- a quantifier with no fact for its variable beside another thing
- a quantifier that says no variable differs from another and holds a condition
- a quantifier whose condition is not about its variable
- a quantifier with several conditions, one of which begins with a time phrase
note: "unless it is one of these" instead of five negations

ideal: There can be three documents A, B and C, with C different from A, where A extends B, B extends C, and C is context for A.
note: short letter names for the chain

ideal: It must be possible that a document starts with a listing frontmatter that lists an installed plugin, checker runs the plugin over the document, and a run calls the plugin, gets code 1 from it, and exits with code 1.
note: told as one story from document to exit code

ideal: When a unit that is not a term holds a formula that no other formula can contradict, checker reports that formula as lone on some signature.
note: the term condition folded into the noun phrase

ideal: When checker reports that a scenario cannot happen, its report names each unit whose leaving out lets the scenario happen.
note: "each unit" carries the universal

ideal: When the statement of a unit is current, checker does not write it when it generates.
note: "it" for the repeated statement

ideal: When a reading in some unit says a word and no unit declares it, the word is a word that a reading says and nothing declares.
note: one sentence, no numbered names

ideal: When an exception cites no fact, checker reports a freelancing for it.
note: "it" for the exception

ideal: When a bug names an issue that tracker has closed, checker reports an outdated tracking for the bug.
note: already plain; only "For every" dropped

ideal: A list can be a rule whose second side begins with a time phrase without being a rule whose two sides are each one clause.
note: "without being" for the negated term
